A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VICON research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: V3 reports original fluid-dynamics forecasting experiments, comparisons with DPOT and MPP, ablations, and robustness analyses in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds a ViT comparison, incorrect-context experiments, and an analysis of physical-field variability.

M1.justification: Patch embedding, positional encodings, block-causal attention, training loss, prompt normalization, and rollout Algorithms 1-5 are retained. Expanded explanations and suggested caching or artifact remedies do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: The same three fluid datasets and forecasting tasks remain. Table 3 adds distinct input conditions on PDEArena-Incomp: mixed-stride, incorrect-stride, and random-noise context pairs, extending the existing missing-frame and sampling-rate scenarios.

E2.justification: V4 Section 5.3 adds an evaluated non-in-context ViT baseline with 162M parameters on PDEArena-Incomp. DPOT and MPP retain their participation in the existing comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include training the ViT control at stride 1 and testing at strides 1 and 2, manipulating context correctness, and comparing field statistics across early and late frames. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 substantially expands mechanism testing through a non-context baseline and incorrect-context controls. New Appendix D.2 investigates already-visible checkerboard artifacts using temporal field statistics. These add distinct mechanism and failure-analysis questions beyond the retained design ablations.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The new standard deviations in Table 10 describe variability of physical fields across time, rather than uncertainty in estimated model performance.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, joint-training, timing, and plotted results are unchanged. Targeted additions include ViT last-step errors of 73.94 and 95.03 at strides 1 and 2, respectively, in units of 1e-2; context-control errors of 0.55, 0.88, 0.92, and 1.57; and Table 10's field-variability statistics.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(13), the temporally homogeneous Markovian assumptions, and mathematical formulation remain unchanged. The added computational-cost discussion informally explains consequences of quadratic attention without introducing a formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient dense-field operator learning, flexible strides, measurement robustness, and the same headline accuracy and runtime improvements. New experiments support retained claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations of checkerboard artifacts through rapid velocity decay and training-inference normalization mismatch. Section 5.7 qualifies measured efficiency with estimated paired-token overhead under matched settings and discusses caching. The conclusion adds concrete possible remedies for existing scaling and rollout limitations.

D1.justification: V4 explicitly states the initial ten-frame rollout input across datasets, clarifies the source of the PDEArena split and positional-encoding broadcasting, and documents the new ViT control's architecture and training stride. Existing VICON hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references to CViT, Message Passing Neural PDE Solvers, and PDE-Transformer, chiefly to motivate possible future extensions. The existing related-work discussion and positioning relative to ICON, DPOT, and MPP are retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are preserved. Changes comprise local language corrections, expanded methodological explanations, and insertion of Sections 5.3 and D.2 with corresponding renumbering.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a different document-wide template with changed typography, margins, and running headers. It redraws Figure 1, adds three tables, relocates table captions, and resizes or redistributes existing displays, including placing Figures 9 and 10 on separate pages. Existing result graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens evidence that VICON uses its context through Table 3 and improves transparency about visible artifacts and computational tradeoffs in Appendix D.2 and Section 5.7. These are useful, targeted gains. The ViT control differs in architecture and training strides, and proposed artifact remedies remain untested, limiting the strength of the additional conclusions.
